99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: I had only ever seen members of the Royal Council in this room before. Today, though, it was packed with military staff. Every single top-ranking general and admiral in Rizia was in attendance.

100.speaker: Player_Romus
100.text: "Let's cut the chit-chat and start with this."

102.speaker: Narrator
102.text: As soon as I entered the room, they stopped their chatter and saluted me. Everyone, except for one man in a wheelchair, General Taddeus Azaro, stood up.

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: They were standing over a massive table, arranging golden and silver tokens atop a map of Pales.

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: The General looked much the same as he had at the football game some months ago.

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: I tried to summon memories of him as my father's war councilor. It was hard to reconcile that authoritative, energetic figure with the frail old man before me.

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: I tried to summon memories of serving alongside him on my father's council. It was hard to reconcile that authoritative, energetic figure with the frail old man before me.

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: I tried to summon memories of my time serving beneath him in the military. It was hard to reconcile that authoritative, energetic figure with the frail old man before me.

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: I locked eyes with Taddeus. He saluted me with a trembling hand.

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: Everyone in the room returned the salute with full force.

124.speaker: Lucita Azaro
124.text: "As the highest-ranking officer in the Rizian Armed Forces and an unmatched expert in military strategy, I invited my father to join us today."

130.speaker: Player_Romus
130.text: "Yes. What are we even waiting for?"

131.speaker: Lucita Azaro
131.text: "Your Majesty, our forces are already mobilized. Our navy and air forces are prepared and awaiting your orders. And our ground forces will be ready to cross the border within 48 hours."

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "What is our intelligence regarding Pales' defenses?"

133.speaker: Player_Romus
133.text: "And what is the plan for the initial strike?"

135.speaker: Lucita Azaro
135.text: "Our intelligence suggests Pales may not be completely prepared for an immediate incursion. We have the element of surprise, which we should capitalize on."

145.speaker: Lucita Azaro
145.text: "Our intelligence suggests Pales is expecting an immediate incursion."

146.speaker: Lucita Azaro
146.text: "However, they have been strengthening their northern border with us -- building forts and bunkers along the River Alca."

159.speaker: Lucita Azaro
159.text: "They have been strengthening their northern border with us -- building forts and bunkers along the River Alca."

160.speaker: Lucita Azaro
160.text: "We also received intelligence about the deployment of dozens of high-tech armored vehicles with unknown capabilities -- which we believe to be of Lespian origin."

161.speaker: Lucita Azaro
161.text: "We believe they've recently received dozens of tanks of Lespian origin as well."

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: She pointed at the Antacean Sea on the map.

163.speaker: Lucita Azaro
163.text: "According to our intelligence, they have already called the ships that were blockading the Aureus field back to the Palesian coasts."

167.speaker: Lucita Azaro
167.text: "Unfortunately, due to their recent acquisition of a large number of Lespian destroyers, their navy is more than capable of breaking our blockade attempts."

168.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
168.text: "The general staff proposes a two-pronged attack. First, we'll need to block Palesian ports, crippling their trade and preventing the Grand Duchy from receiving any external support."

169.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
169.text: "Second, we'll mount a large ground offensive aimed at securing key border defenses."

171.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
171.text: "Speed is of the essence. We must overwhelm Palesian soldiers before they can fully mobilize."

172.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
172.text: "However, an assault from the north --particularly across the Alca -- would come at a high cost, as it remains their most heavily fortified border."

176.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
176.text: "However, an assault from the north would be a tough endeavor, especially given the difficulties of crossing the Alca."

189.speaker: Lucita Azaro
189.text: "Unfortunately, due to their recent acquisition of a large number of Lespian destroyers, their navy is more than capable of breaking our blockade attempts."

190.speaker: Lucita Azaro
190.text: "And according to reports, they are already deploying thousands of soldiers along their entire border at this moment."

191.speaker: Player_Romus
191.text: "Okay. Let's talk about our deployment and general strategy."

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "If we attack from the north, we could catch them by surprise. They wouldn't expect us to lead a grand offensive on their most fortified border."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "How about striking from their western border?"

199.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
199.text: "Our proposal is to feign an attack in the north to make them focus their forces there, but to spread our forces throughout the border."

200.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
200.text: "This strategy would allow us to strike from the west."

201.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
201.text: "We could feign an attack in the north to drawn their forces there, while we concentrate the majority of our forces in the west."

202.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
202.text: "However, their western border is covered with mountains. And we believe they possess specially trained mountaineer units defending that terrain."

203.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
203.text: "There is a chance we can break through from their southern coast with the help of our navy."

204.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
204.text: "If we can deploy our armored units on that front, we can push from their coast and block their supply lines."

205.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
205.text: "It is indeed one of our options."

211.speaker: Player_Romus
211.text: "What would attacking from the north entail?"

212.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
212.text: "We would deploy our armored forces around Fort Ales and focus our attack on Navar."

216.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
216.text: "If we get Navar quickly, we can move towards Arces and cut the supply lines for their whole army."

217.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
217.text: "However, initiating an attack from Fort Ales would put our city at great risk. And we have to be quick enough for them not to focus their forces in the north."

218.speaker: Player_Romus
218.text: "We can also focus on a naval invasion."

219.speaker: Player_Romus
219.text: "I like the idea to feign an attack from the north to split their forces."

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "I think this is the strategy they would least expect."

225.speaker: Player_Romus
225.text: "I think we shouldn't risk anything with a fake assault."

226.speaker: Lucita Azaro
226.text: "I'm afraid with our current capabilities, it is not possible to initiate a massive naval invasion."

227.speaker: Lucita Azaro
227.text: "Our specially trained marines can definitely open an additional front from the south, but due to our capacity, it would be a quite limited assault."

228.speaker: Lucita Azaro
228.text: "I'm afraid with our current capabilities, it is not possible to initiate any meaningful naval invasion."

229.speaker: Lucita Azaro
229.text: "Although our navy could potentially support our land units in the south, we do not possess the capability to carry enough troops for a successful landing."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "What would attacking from the north entail?"

236.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
236.text: "I'm with you on that, Your Majesty."

237.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
237.text: "If they do not possess our deployment plans, that might force them to keep a balanced defense throughout their border."

238.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
238.text: "I suspect that to be the case as well, Your Majesty."

239.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
239.text: "As the King, you have total control over our military strategy and the deployment of our troops."

240.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
240.text: "However, I've prepared a briefing that will help inform your decisions. Would you like to hear it?"

243.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
243.text: "What would you like to hear about first?"

249.speaker: Narrator
249.text: The room fell into a silence as everybody looked at me in anticipation of what I would say next.

250.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
250.text: "Your Majesty. As the King, you have total control over our military strategy and the deployment of our troops."

252.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
252.text: "But before you give the orders, would you like to hear about the status of our military and the options the generals outlined?"

254.speaker: Player_Romus
254.text: "No. I already know everything, General. I'm ready to give you your orders, so listen carefully."

256.speaker: Narrator
256.text: His face contorted in silent anger, but he refrained from responding to me and bowed his head.

261.speaker: Lucita Azaro
261.text: "Due to the extensive Palesian naval defenses around Pales and the Gulf of Ales -- as well as the possibility of direct engagement with Lespia -- our strategy will have to rely on an attack from either the north or the southwest."

262.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
262.text: "Our first objective is to take control of the cities of Ziqes and Arces and trap their forces at the chokepoint at Solles."

263.speaker: Player_Romus
263.text: "Give me the details of each front and what to expect."

266.speaker: Player_Romus
266.text: "We will lead a direct assault without any precursors. It is better if they spread their defenses without a clear focus."

267.speaker: Player_Romus
267.text: "Before the invasion, we will feign an attack from the north and try to get their forces to focus there."

268.speaker: Player_Romus
268.text: "Before the invasion, we will feign an attack from the south and try to get their forces to focus there."

269.speaker: Narrator
269.text: The generals in the room gave me a military salute while shouting "Yes, sir."

270.speaker: Player_Romus
270.text: "I will look into it in detail, General."

271.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
271.text: "In light of this, I'd like to send you a detailed plan for our initial deployment through the border -- focusing on a simultaneous attack toward Ziqes and the southwestern coast."

272.speaker: Player_Romus
272.text: "No offense, general, but I'll plan the assault and the deployment of our forces personally."

273.speaker: Player_Romus
273.text: "I cannot, and will not, oversee every division or the entire war effort. I will grant full authority for the invasion to the General Staff and to you, General Azaro." [OPT OUT OF WAR GAMEPLAY]

276.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
276.text: "Our initial operation will be aimed at taking control of Arces and Ziqes."

277.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
277.text: "The city of Ziqes is located very close to our borders, and it lies on the highway and railway system that runs through the middle of the country."

278.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
278.text: "Due to the city's proximity to our borders, it is heavily defended. Unfortunately, our air forces will only be of help once we destroy their anti-air systems, which are located in the mountains south of the city."

279.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
279.text: "Another strategic point is the town of Navar, directly by our border near Fort Ales."

280.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
280.text: "Pales also has incredibly sophisticated anti-air defenses installed in that area -- and any attack from the north would require the capture of the area for our air forces to be able to support our operation."

282.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
282.text: "The most important goal for our initial operation is to capture the city of Arces, situated directly in the middle of Pales."

283.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
283.text: "We have intelligence that their defense is organized from there and it provides supplies to every front. By cutting that city from their network, we can crush their border defenses and create a new frontline from Navar to the sea."

297.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
297.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option3"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option1"] == true) == false

298.speaker: Player_Romus
298.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option3"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option1"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_PrepareForWar"] == true) == false)

299.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
299.text: "What are your initial orders, Your Majesty?"

300.speaker: Player_Romus
300.text: "Furthermore, we will keep our navy on standby until the assault begins. We cannot risk any reckless damage."

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "Furthermore, we will immediately focus our Navy to blockade the Gulf of Ales. It is their most heavily guarded area but the closest to our coastline."

302.speaker: Player_Romus
302.text: "Furthermore, we will immediately focus our Navy to blockade the Gulf of Pales. Our efforts must be focused at their capital even if that means a direct confrontation with their strongest fleet."

303.speaker: Player_Romus
303.text: "Furthermore, we will immediately focus our Navy to blockade the Gulf of Remaz. Our efforts must be focused on disrupting their trade without a risky confrontation at sea."

371.speaker: Player_Romus
371.text: "We will keep our navy and our marines on standby for a possible naval invasion. We cannot risk any reckless damage before the invasion begins."

375.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
375.text: "As mentioned, our ground forces are mobilizing as we speak, Your Majesty."

382.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
382.text: "We can field a substantial number of infantry divisions, which are quite enough to overwhelm the Palesian forces."

383.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
383.text: "We can field approximately eight to nine fully equipped infantry divisions. This should be a solid force for our campaign against Pales.

384.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
384.text: "We can field approximately six to seven fully equipped infantry divisions. Given our modest numbers, we must exercise caution, as infantry makes up the bulk of our forces."

385.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
385.text: We can field five fully equipped infantry divisions, but with Palesian infantry outnumbering us, we should proceed with caution."

395.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
395.text: "Fortunately, we have a significant number of mechanized support divisions, which will prove invaluable in backing up our infantry and armored divisions during the assault."

396.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
396.text: "Fortunately, we have a solid number of mechanized support divisions, which will provide vital assistance in supporting the infantry and armored divisions during their assaults."

397.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
397.text: "On the other hand, we also have a modest number of mechanized support divisions which will be useful in supporting the assaults of our infantry and armored divisions."

398.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
398.text: "Unfortunately, we can only field three mechanized support divisions, each specifically trained to assist the assaults of our infantry and armored divisions.

399.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
399.text: "We should not risk losing them -- as they can change the tide of the war."

400.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
400.text: "And lastly, when it comes to our tanks..."

410.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
410.text: "Our tank divisions outnumber Pales' and will spearhead the main assault."

411.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
411.text: "We currently field enough tank divisions to spearhead the main assault."

412.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
412.text: "I hate to say it, but Pales has far more than we have. We can only field three tank divisions."

413.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
413.text: "I hate to say it, but Pales has far more than we have. We can barely field two tank divisions."

415.speaker: Lucita Azaro
415.text: "Meanwhile, our air force stands ready to challenge Palesian control of the skies."

419.speaker: Lucita Azaro
419.text: "On the other hand, our air force is barely capable of contesting Palesian air superiority."

423.speaker: Lucita Azaro
423.text: "Our admirals have reported that our specially trained marine divisions and their deployment ships will be ready to initiate a coastal invasion in no time."

427.speaker: Lucita Azaro
427.text: "And lastly, our navy is led by our flagship RRN Valero."

428.speaker: Lucita Azaro
428.text: "And lastly, our navy has unfortunately suffered a great loss with RRN Valero taken out of service."

429.speaker: Lucita Azaro
429.text: "It is also important to highlight that despite the great investments Rizia has made in our navy, the Palesians still have access to superior technology."

430.speaker: Lucita Azaro
430.text: "It is also important to highlight that while we can theoretically hold our own against the Palesian navy, they boast both superior technology and larger numbers."

440.speaker: Lucita Azaro
440.text: "Luckily, our fleets contain a large number of destroyers -- which will surely help us gain superiority at sea."

441.speaker: Lucita Azaro
441.text: "Our fleets also contain enough destroyers to be able to contest the Palesian navy at critical locations."

442.speaker: Lucita Azaro
442.text: "Unfortunately, we do not have enough fleets to be able to counter Palesian ships in any direct confrontation."

446.speaker: Lucita Azaro
446.text: "Our submarines will also provide support when necessary. We have enough of them to be able to wreak havoc on Pales' ships."

447.speaker: Lucita Azaro
447.text: "Our submarines will also provide support when necessary. Although we don't have many of them, they can still wreak havoc on Pales' ships."

453.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
453.text: "On their northern border, they have several heavily fortified areas across the River Alca."

454.speaker: Narrator
454.text: He pointed to the River Alca on our border with Pales.

455.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
455.text: "They also have sophisticated air defenses placed around the town of Navar -- very close to our city, Fort Ales."

456.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
456.text: "These defenses will severely impact our capability to push for an assault from Fort Ales."

457.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
457.text: "Their most defended position on their western front is right between Rizia's Terador and the Palesian city of Ziqes."

458.speaker: Narrator
458.text: He then pointed to the border city of Ziqes.

459.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
459.text: "We suspect they may push for a counter offensive from Ziqes -- possibly with their armored divisions in the front."

460.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
460.text: "The city of Ziqes and its surroundings are also defended by heavy air defense systems -- which we believe to be located south of the city."

461.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
461.text: "The western border features rugged mountainous terrain, effectively dividing Pales by separating the northern front from the south."

462.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
462.text: "As previously mentioned, we anticipate fierce resistance in these mountains, as we believe Pales has specialized mountaineer units stationed to defend those positions."

465.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
465.text: "Yes, Your Majesty. Thank you for your confidence."

466.speaker: Lucita Azaro
466.text: "We will relay your orders immediately, Your Majesty."

467.speaker: Narrator
467.text: Everyone in the room -- except Taddeus -- stood up and saluted me.

468.speaker: Lucita Azaro
468.text: "I will return to you as soon as we have an update."

469.speaker: Narrator
469.text: And there it was. The Invasion of Pales was about to begin.

475.speaker: Player_Romus
475.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option3"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option1"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_PrepareForWar"] == true)

480.speaker: Lucita Azaro
480.text: "Before we begin, some news from our Grand Admiral..."

484.speaker: Lucita Azaro
484.text: "Unfortunately, the damage from the attack on our flagship Valero were worse than initially reported and the ship remains out of service. We won't be able to use it in our invasion."

485.speaker: Narrator
485.text: She directed our attention to the map on the table.

512.speaker: Narrator
512.text: The last time I had seen the room this full was at the start of the Reclamation War. Now, just like then, it was packed with military staff. Every single top-ranking general and admiral in Rizia was in attendance.

513.speaker: Narrator
513.text: The people assembled in the room relaxed their shoulders slightly, but kept their backs straight.

518.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
518.text: "Good form for a civilian, Your Majesty."

519.speaker: Narrator
519.text: He moved his lips wordlessly, then finally spoke.

523.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
523.text: "Glad to be of service, Your Majesty."

524.speaker: Player_Romus
524.text: "You answer to me now. Don't forget that."

526.speaker: Player_Romus
526.text: "I must commend your daughter for her exceptional performance on the Council in your stead."

527.speaker: Player_Romus
527.text: "My apologies. You shouldn't have been dragged out of your sickbed for this."

528.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
528.text: "Never, Your Majesty. I will endeavor to serve you just as I served your father, God rest his soul."

529.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
529.text: "Better by the day. I knew there was a reason death spared me. To help Rizia retake Pales once and for all."

534.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
534.text: "I dragged myself here, Your Majesty. Death spared me for a single reason: to help Rizia retake Pales once and for all."

535.speaker: Narrator
535.text: He slowly smiled as his gaze drifted between the two of us. Lucita cleared her throat.

536.speaker: Lucita Azaro
536.text: "But according to reports, they are already deploying thousands of soldiers along their entire border at this moment."

537.speaker: Narrator
537.text: Taddeus gestured for one of his aides to bring him a pointer. He aimed it at the map.

variablesModified.value: "The resulting massive boost in manpower is sure to give us an edge in the fight to liberate Pales."

539.speaker: Narrator
539.text: Lucita turned her attention to General Azaro.

540.speaker: Lucita Azaro
540.text: "His ailment may have slowed his stride, but his mind remains as sharp as ever."

541.speaker: Narrator
541.text: Standing next to them was General Carlos Robles Azaro, the second-in-command of the Armed Forces, best known for his defense of Porte Drazon during the Uprising.

542.speaker: Narrator
542.text: Unlike his superior, Carlos stood with an air of energy and vigor, his posture straight and alert as he saluted me once more.

546.speaker: Player_Romus
546.text: "There he is. The man. The legend."

551.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
551.text: "Thank you, Your Majesty. The honor is mine."

552.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
552.text: “Hardly, Your Majesty. Just a soldier doing his duty.”

553.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
553.text: "Too long, Your Majesty. I'm honored to be here."

554.speaker: Carlos Robles Azaro
554.text: "Thank you, Your Majesty. It's an honor to be here."

555.speaker: Lucita Azaro
555.text: "We can conduct bombings almost everywhere outside of the reach of their primary air defense systems -- which are not insignificant to say the least."

556.speaker: Lucita Azaro
556.text: "We can still try conducting bombings outside of the reach of their primary air defense systems -- which will be quite a problem."

557.speaker: Narrator
557.text: The generals exchanged brief glances, a silent confirmation passing between them.

560.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
560.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option4"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn06_WarBriefing_Hub2_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Enable_Policy_RD_Order_RemoveProvincialLevies"] == false) == false

561.speaker: Player_Romus
561.text: "And what of our provincial House forces?"

562.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
562.text: "As for the House units themselves, I’m proud to say that House Azaro’s forces are the best organized and excel in offensive operations."

563.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
563.text: "As for House Sazon... while their ability to launch sustained assaults is limited, their troops are highly organized and provide the strongest land-based logistical support."

564.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
564.text: "Meanwhile, House Toras maintains a well-balanced force with strong defensive capabilities."

565.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
565.text: "Our defensive capabilities may not be as robust as some other Houses, but they are more than capable in swift, decisive strikes."

566.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
566.text: "However, like House Sazon, their offensive strength is better suited for support roles than for spearheading an attack."

570.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
570.text: "Thanks to your order to increase provincial levies, I’m proud to report that the size of our House army divisions has effectively doubled."

571.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
571.text: This policy has greatly enhanced our military strength, providing us with both additional manpower and crucial equipment to better support our operations."

572.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
572.text: "You'll be pleased to know that units comprising House troops are among the most capable in the Rizian Armed Forces."

573.speaker: Taddeus Azaro
573.text: "All in all, should they face Palesian troops, each House will prove to be a formidable fighting force."
